title: COVID-19 Serology Surveys in Resource-Limited Settings
author: Farid, Jusril, et al.

steps.title: Send invitations and assign venues
steps.instruction: For districts with a laboratory, have the laboratory district invite selected respondents to the designated venue; for districts without a laboratory, have the district invite respondents to the assigned venue (village hall or community health centre) and arrange transport of specimens to the laboratory. The head of the village or primary health service provider staff sends the invitation before the D‑day. If a respondent’s schedule conflicts, reschedule to another date at the other venue within the same district.

steps.title: Prepare venue layout and tables
steps.instruction: On the D‑day set up several tables in the venue in the following order: (1) identity verification and consent table, (2) specimen collection table, (3) interview table. Ensure tables are clearly labeled and spaced for smooth participant flow.

steps.title: Verify identity and obtain consent
steps.instruction: At the identity verification table, field personnel confirm each respondent’s ID, explain the study, and obtain written consent from the respondent or guardian.

steps.title: Collect blood sample
steps.instruction: Direct the consented respondent to the specimen collection table and draw approximately 3–6 mL of blood by venepuncture.

steps.title: Conduct questionnaire interview
steps.instruction: After blood collection, have the respondent proceed to the interview table where an enumerator administers a paper‑based questionnaire.

steps.title: Enter data into web application
steps.instruction: The enumerator enters questionnaire responses and laboratory data into the web‑based application, which applies initial data checking with skip logic. Depending on network strength, data entry can be performed at the collection venue or at another designated venue on the D‑day.

steps.title: Transport specimens to laboratory
steps.instruction: For districts without an on‑site laboratory, transport the collected blood specimens to the designated laboratory as arranged.
